results.title: Foreign investors favor PT Bumi Resources Minerals Tbk (BRMS), PT Merdeka Gold Resources Tbk (EMAS) and PT Adaro Andalan Indonesia Tbk (AADI); Top 10 Net‑Buy Stocks of the Week
results.body: During the week of 14–18 September 2026, foreign investors recorded net purchases in ten Indonesian stocks, with PT Bumi Resources Minerals Tbk (BRMS), PT Merdeka Gold Resources Tbk (EMAS) and PT Adaro Andalan Indonesia Tbk (AADI) leading the list. Net‑buy values were Rp324.7 billion for BRMS, Rp122.9 billion for EMAS, Rp115 billion for AADI, Rp92.3 billion for PT Amman Mineral Internasional Tbk (AMMN), Rp74.9 billion for PT Erajaya Swasembada Tbk (ERAA), Rp43.3 billion for PT Archi Indonesia Tbk (ARCI), Rp33.3 billion for PT Perusahaan Gas Negara Tbk (PGAS), Rp30.3 billion for PT Bukit Asam Tbk (PTBA), Rp28.9 billion for PT Aneka Tambang Tbk (ANTM) and Rp22 billion for PT Telkom Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (TLKM). Overall foreign‑investor activity was a net sell of Rp1.84 trillion, coinciding with the IHSG index falling 1.53 % to 6,441,159, market‑capitalization decreasing 1.58 % to Rp11,266 trillion, and average daily transaction value, frequency and volume all declining. Analysts linked the market pressure to a 25‑basis‑point Fed rate hike to a 3.75‑4 % target range and expectations of further increases, which have been priced into the market.

results.title: BAKN DPR RI Urges Government to Prepare Backup Plan for PT Kereta Cepat Indonesia China Debt Transfer as September 15 Deadline Looms
results.body: The State Financial Accountability Agency (BAKN) of the House of Representatives has urged the government to prepare a contingency plan for the debt transfer of PT Kereta Cepat Indonesia China, operator of the Whoosh high-speed rail, as the September 15 settlement target appears unlikely to be met. Chairman Andreas Eddy Susetyo warned that ongoing due diligence may not conclude in time, potentially burdening PT Kereta Api Indonesia financially. Finance Minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa previously disclosed the restructured debt carries an annual installment of approximately Rp1 trillion with a tenor of up to 80 years. Separately, BAKN pressed Danantara, as shareholder of PT Kereta Api Indonesia and PT Bukit Asam, to strengthen supervision following recurring Supreme Audit Agency findings at state-owned enterprises.

results.title: Mirae Asset Sekuritas assesses global pressures still weighing on the market
results.body: Mirae Asset Sekuritas says global sentiment continues to weigh on Indonesia’s market, noting that the Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) fell 1.33% to 6,589 amid a net foreign outflow of Rp748 billion. The pressure was most evident on banking stocks BBCA and BBRI, while foreign investors accumulated commodity‑linked shares such as ANTM, AADI, CUAN and PTBA. The firm cites macro factors including the US 10‑year Treasury yield near 5%, the ECB rate at 2.5%, high oil prices, the rupiah at roughly Rp17,547 per USD and a 10‑year SBN yield of 7.11% as limiting the transmission of global yields to the domestic market. Despite these headwinds, consumer confidence rose to 118.5 in August and Mirae Asset recommends a selective portfolio focused on strong fundamentals and solid cash flow.

results.title: Foreign Investor Outflow Rp590 Billion, Two Prajogo Pangestu‑Affiliated Stocks Lead Net Sell
results.body: Foreign investors recorded a net outflow of Rp590.18 billion on Monday, with the market turning to net sell positions. The top net‑sell stocks were PT Chandra Asri Pacific Tbk (Rp121.2 billion, 61.03 million shares) and PT Petrindo Jaya Kreasi Tbk (Rp87.9 billion, 93.60 million shares), followed by PT Indosat Tbk (Rp64.8 billion, 27.53 million shares), PT Kalbe Farma Tbk (Rp62.3 billion, 77.91 million shares) and PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (Rp53.7 billion, 12.21 million shares); the two leading losers are affiliated with Prajogo Pangestu. On the buy side, PT Bumi Resources Tbk led with a net buy of Rp180.5 billion and 830 million shares, while PT Bukit Asam Tbk, PT Adaro Andalan Indonesia Tbk, PT MNC Energy Investments Tbk and PT Puradelta Lestari Tbk recorded net buys of Rp52.2 billion, Rp38.1 billion, Rp31.6 billion and Rp27.2 billion respectively, with volumes of 173.9 million, 3.26 million, 230 million and 130 million shares.

results.title: PT Bukit Asam Tbk targets 20% non‑coal revenue share by 2030 and reports H1 2026 net profit of Rp4.06 trillion
results.body: PT Bukit Asam Tbk said it will increase the contribution of non‑coal and green‑energy revenue to 20% of total earnings by 2030, up from about 3% currently. The plan relies on securing 842 million tonnes of coal reserves for a 20‑year supply and on constructing gasification projects for dimethyl ether (DME) and synthetic natural gas (SNG) with physical completion targeted for 2027. DME will be off‑taken by Pertamina Patra Niaga for LPG substitution and SNG will be supplied to PGN for industrial gas, both under the National Strategic Projects coordinated by Danantara, while PTBA will also expand its 1.2 MWp solar portfolio through cooperation with Pertamina NRE and participation in PLN’s RUPTL auction. The company reported H1 2026 revenue of Rp22.03 trillion and net profit of Rp4.06 trillion, a 4.2‑times year‑on‑year rise.

results.title: PT Bukit Asam Tbk reports 218% YoY net profit jump to Rp 2.65 trillion in H1 2026
results.body: PT Bukit Asam Tbk posted a net profit of Rp 2.65 trillion for the first half of 2026, a 218% year‑on‑year increase. Revenue rose 8% YoY to Rp 22.03 trillion, supported by a 10% rise in average selling price of coal and stronger export sales. Coal production reached 19.45 million tons and sales totaled 21.1 million tons, with exports of 10.33 million tons (up 5%) to Vietnam, Bangladesh, Cambodia, India and Thailand, while domestic sales accounted for about 51% of volume. The company aims to hit its target of roughly 50 million tons of production and sales by year‑end 2026, buoyed by global coal price gains reflected in the Newcastle Index (+25% YoY) and ICI‑3 (+15% YoY).

results.title: PT Bukit Asam Tbk targets non‑coal and coal‑derivative businesses to contribute about 20% of revenue within three to four years
results.body: PT Bukit Asam Tbk announced that its non‑coal and coal‑derivative segments are expected to generate roughly 20 % of the company's total revenue within the next three to four years. To achieve this, the firm is advancing downstream projects including coal‑to‑dimethyl ether (DME), methanol, synthetic natural gas (SNG), potassium humate, artificial graphite and solar power, with DME construction slated to start in 2027. A pilot coal‑to‑potassium humate plant will begin with about 100 tons capacity and aims to scale to 10 000 tons per year, while the artificial graphite project is pursued with Badan Riset dan Inovasi Nasional for battery‑industry use. PT Bukit Asam Tbk will also work with Danantara on a coal‑to‑SNG project as part of its diversification strategy.

results.title: The Fate of Bukit Asam (PTBA)
results.body: The article examines the sharp rebound in PT Bukit Asam Tbk shares, which gapped up 4.51% to Rp 3,010 in the first session on 7 September 2026, driven by heavy foreign net buying and a turnaround in first-half earnings. Foreign investors purchased a net 13 million shares worth Rp 38.91 billion in the session, extending a weekly net buy of Rp 57.97 billion for 31 August–4 September, a jump from Rp 4.84 billion the prior week. The rally followed PTBA's 1H26 results showing revenue of Rp 22.03 trillion (+8% year-on-year), net profit of Rp 2.65 trillion, and EBITDA of Rp 4.27 trillion, with margins of 12% and 19% respectively. Operational recovery in the second quarter saw production surge 94% quarter-on-quarter and sales rise 8%, while the average selling price climbed 14% sequentially, supported by a 25% rise in the Newcastle Index and 15% rise in ICI-3. The company's capital expenditure reached 30% of its annual target at Rp 1.09 trillion by end-June, with export sales accounting for 49% of the mix, primarily to Vietnam, Bangladesh, Cambodia, India, and Thailand.

results.title: IHSG Predicted Mixed on Monday (Sept 7), Investors Cautioned on Rupiah and US‑Iran Conflict
results.body: Analysts forecast that Indonesia's composite stock index (IHSG) will trade within a narrow range of 6,580–6,700 on Monday, with support at 6,580–6,600 and resistance at 6,680–6,700 amid mixed sentiment. They cite foreign net buying of roughly Rp1.6 trillion in the past week, a Rupiah level near Rp17,642 per USD, and Brent crude around US$95 per barrel as factors that could influence the index while monitoring Fed policy cues and the US‑Iran conflict. Specific equities highlighted as potential drivers include PT Bukit Asam Tbk (target Rp3,100), PT Petrindo Jaya Kreasi Tbk (target Rp1,100), PT Bumi Resources Tbk (target Rp250), PT Sinergi Inti Andalan Prima Tbk (target Rp400), PT Petrosea Tbk (buy on break at Rp5,500, resistance Rp5,950) and PT Timah Tbk (trading buy with support Rp4,150, resistance Rp4,720). The outlook remains sensitive to any shift in US labor data, Treasury yields, or escalation of tensions in the Strait of Hormuz, which could affect energy stocks and overall market sentiment.

results.title: PT Bukit Asam Tbk reports strong 1H 2026 earnings and 13.8% share price rise on foreign net buying
results.body: PT Bukit Asam Tbk, a state‑owned coal producer (BUMN), reported a strong first‑half 2026 performance, with revenue of Rp 22.03 trillion up 8% YoY and net profit of Rp 2.65 trillion, delivering a 12% net profit margin and 19% EBITDA margin. Production rose 94% QoQ and sales increased 8% QoQ, while average selling price grew 14% QoQ and 10% YoY, supported by a 49% export share to Vietnam, Bangladesh, Cambodia, India and Thailand. Foreign investors accumulated a net buy of Rp 57.97 billion in the week of 31 Aug–4 Sep 2026, driving the share price to jump 13.83% and close at Rp 2,880, a 24.14% gain over the past month. Capital expenditure reached 30% of the annual target, amounting to Rp 1.09 trillion.

results.title: Foreign investors' top ten net‑buy stocks on 4 Sep 2026 amid a 0.47% IHSG correction
results.body: The article reports that foreign investors net bought ten Indonesian stocks on Friday 4 Sep 2026 while the Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) corrected 0.47% to 6,636.47. The market closed within a range of 6,633–6,704, with total share volume of 35.8 billion and transaction value of Rp 15.04 trillion, and foreign investors recorded a net sell of Rp 29.80 billion that day. Over the week, foreign investors accumulated a net buy of Rp 1.85 trillion, and the ten most purchased stocks were PT Dian Swastatika Sentosa Tbk (Rp 196.83 billion), PT Timah Tbk (Rp 158.76 billion), PT Adaro Andalan Indonesia Tbk (Rp 46.47 billion), PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia Tbk (Rp 33.6 billion), PT Chandra Daya Investasi Tbk (Rp 25.27 billion), PT Bank Negara Indonesia Tbk (Rp 24.54 billion), PT Merdeka Gold Resources Tbk (Rp 24.45 billion), PT Bukit Asam Tbk (Rp 19.11 billion), PT Sumber Global Energy Tbk (Rp 13.25 billion) and PT United Tractors Tbk (Rp 10.43 billion). These companies were directly impacted by the foreign investors' net purchases, while the IHSG still posted a weekly gain of 1.82% despite the weekend correction.

results.title: Energy sector stays a market primadona as analysts recommend PT Alamtri Resources Indonesia Tbk and PT Bukit Asam Tbk
results.body: The IDX Energy index rose 1.36% to 3,364.14 on 3 September 2026, marking a 14.16% gain for the month and underscoring the sector’s continued strength. Analysts Hendra Wardana and Sukarno Alatas attribute the momentum to improving fundamentals, commodity price support, and production recovery in the second half of 2026. Wardana recommends PT Alamtri Resources Indonesia Tbk, an emiten, as a trading buy with a target price of Rp2,860 per share. He also recommends PT Bukit Asam Tbk, an emiten, as a trading buy with a target price of Rp3,000 per share.

results.title: Ten Indonesian coal issuers report H1 2026 net profit growth led by Adaro Andalan Indonesia Tbk and Bayan Resources Tbk
results.body: Ten Indonesian coal mining issuers posted year-on-year net profit increases in the first half of 2026, with PT Adaro Andalan Indonesia Tbk recording the highest profit attributable to parent entity owners at US$473.77 million (approximately Rp8.48 trillion), up 10.52%, followed by PT Bayan Resources Tbk at approximately Rp7.34 trillion, up 17.47%. PT Alamtri Resources Indonesia Tbk ranked third with US$309.36 million (Rp5.54 trillion), a 76.83% surge, while PT Alamtri Minerals Indonesia Tbk, PT Bukit Asam Tbk, PT Indo Tambangraya Megah Tbk, PT Bumi Resources Tbk, PT Darma Henwa Tbk, PT Petrindo Jaya Kreasi Tbk, and PT Indika Energy Tbk completed the list with profits ranging from Rp3.12 trillion down to Rp182 billion. PT Petrindo Jaya Kreasi Tbk posted the highest profit growth at approximately 918% to US$19.78 million (Rp354 billion), and PT Indika Energy Tbk followed with a 354.30% increase to US$10.20 million (Rp182 billion). Revenue growth accompanied profit gains across the group, with Adaro's revenue rising 6.13% to US$2.55 billion and Bayan's reaching approximately Rp31.15 trillion.

results.title: PT Bukit Asam Tbk reports 218% profit surge in H1 2026; target price under review
results.body: PT Bukit Asam Tbk posted a first‑half 2026 net profit of Rp 2.7 trillion, up 218% year‑on‑year and surpassing both the Indo Premier Sekuritas estimate (73% of target) and the consensus (66%). The earnings surge was driven by a 14% quarterly rise in average selling price for coal, an improved stripping ratio of 5.2 times, and a 61% quarterly increase in joint‑venture revenue to Rp 270 billion, while cash cost rose to Rp 899 000 per ton. Gross profit margin expanded to 22% and EBITDA margin to 19%, with domestic sales accounting for 51% of total volume, of which PT PLN absorbed 7.8 million tons. Indo Premier Sekuritas kept its 2026 earnings outlook but left the PTBA share target of Rp 2 000 under review pending further performance details.

results.title: List of LQ45 stocks with lowest and highest PER on 2 September 2026, highlighting DEWA and AADI
results.body: The article lists the LQ45 index stocks with the lowest and highest price‑earnings ratios (PER) on 2 September 2026, highlighting PT Darma Henwa and PT Adaro Andalan Indonesia. Trading volume fell as the total transaction value dropped to Rp16.8 trillion from Rp20.7 trillion, and foreign investors posted a net sell of 5.59 billion shares worth Rp326.6 billion. PT Adaro Andalan Indonesia declined 2.07% and PT Darma Henwa slipped 2.16%, while PT Amman Mineral Internasional fell 2.06%, PT United Tractors dropped 2.05%, PT Bukit Asam rose 1.87%, and PT Indah Kiat Pulp & Paper held the lowest price‑to‑book value at 0.38 times. PT Japfa Comfeed Indonesia, PT Petrindo Jaya Kreasi, PT Bumi Resources, and PT GoTo Gojek Tokopedia were largely stagnant, and six other LQ45 constituents each weakened by less than 2%, all of which are members of the LQ45 index as noted in the article.

results.title: UBS upgrades PT Bukit Asam Tbk on outlook for large dividend and strong net profit growth
results.body: UBS has upgraded PT Bukit Asam Tbk after projecting a large dividend supported by strong earnings growth. The broker expects net profit to rise 218% to Rp2.7 trillion in the first half of 2026, representing 68% of its full-year forecast and 66% of analyst consensus, and to increase 130% quarter-on-quarter to Rp1.8 trillion in Q2 2026. Sales are forecast to grow 8% with an average selling price up 10%, while cash cost rises only 4%, lifting cash margin to US$11 per ton, the highest in six quarters. UBS also notes that PT Bukit Asam's net cash balance grew to Rp3.9 trillion in Q2 2026 from Rp1.5 trillion in the prior quarter.

results.title: PT Timah Tbk records the most aggressive growth among Indonesian miners in H1 2026, surpassing PT Antam Tbk, PT Bukit Asam Tbk and PT Vale Indonesia Tbk
results.body: PT Timah Tbk posted the strongest performance among Indonesian mining issuers in the MIND ID ecosystem during the first half of 2026, with revenue rising 146.9% to Rp 10.4 trillion and net profit surging 804.6% to Rp 2.7 trillion. In comparison, PT Antam Tbk generated Rp 62.7 trillion of revenue (+6.3%) and Rp 6.39 trillion of net profit (+36.0%); PT Bukit Asam Tbk reported Rp 22.03 trillion of revenue (+7.7%) and Rp 2.65 trillion of net profit (+218%); PT Vale Indonesia Tbk recorded Rp 9.6 trillion of revenue (+27.4%) and Rp 1.85 trillion of net profit (+313.6%). The analyst attributes PT Timah’s outperformance to higher tin prices, increased sales volume, and a low prior profit base, while noting heightened volatility risk. Sustained tin prices and production in the second half of 2026 will be critical for maintaining the momentum.

results.title: PT Bukit Asam Tbk reports 8% YoY revenue growth and 12% net profit margin in 1H 2026
results.body: PT Bukit Asam Tbk announced its consolidated financial results for the six months ended 30 June 2026, showing an 8% year‑on‑year increase in revenue to Rp 22.03 trillion. Net profit reached Rp 2.65 trillion with a net profit margin of 12% and EBITDA of Rp 4.27 trillion, yielding an EBITDA margin of 19%. The company recorded a 94% quarter‑on‑quarter rise in production and an 8% rise in sales, with average selling price up 14% quarter‑on‑quarter and 10% year‑on‑year, while domestic sales accounted for 51% of total revenue and exports 49% to Vietnam, Bangladesh, Kamboja, India and Thailand. Capital expenditure to date covered 30% of the annual target, amounting to Rp 1.09 trillion, reflecting the firm’s continued focus on operational efficiency and market‑driven pricing.

results.title: Global Coal Price Surge Drives Strong First-Half 2026 Earnings for Indonesian Coal Miners
results.body: Rising global coal prices since March 2026 have significantly improved the financial performance of Indonesian coal mining companies in the first half of 2026. PT Bukit Asam Tbk reported revenue growth of 7.73% to Rp 22.03 trillion and a 218.10% surge in net profit to Rp 2.65 trillion, while PT Bumi Resources Tbk saw net profit jump 188.34% to US$58.85 million on 27.85% revenue growth to US$866.75 million. PT Adaro Andalan Indonesia Tbk posted 6.25% revenue growth to US$2.55 billion and a 10.52% rise in net profit to US$473.77 million. Analysts attribute the gains to coal prices above US$120 per ton, operational improvements, and structural demand from AI and seasonal factors, highlighting PT Bukit Asam Tbk, PT Adaro Andalan Indonesia Tbk, ADRO, ADMR, ITMG, and INDY as favored picks for the second half, with trading recommendations for PT Bumi Resources Tbk (Rp 224 target) and INDY (Rp 3,330 target).

results.title: PT Bukit Asam Tbk reports net profit of Rp2.64 trillion, up 218% in the first half of 2026
results.body: PT Bukit Asam Tbk announced a net profit of Rp2.64 trillion for the first semester of 2026, representing a 218.10% year‑over‑year increase. Total revenue rose to Rp22.02 trillion, driven by coal sales of Rp12.3 trillion to third parties and Rp9.36 trillion to related parties, plus Rp355 billion from other activities such as electricity and palm‑oil products. The company also reported a 2.33% decline in cost of goods sold to Rp17.7 trillion, resulting in a gross profit of Rp4.24 trillion, while assets grew to Rp48.1 trillion and equity to Rp25.3 trillion at the end of June 2026.
